fix: the people of Elea and the Neapolitans
reason: Ἐλεατῶν are the Italian Eleates of Elea/Velia, not Eleans of Elis in the Peloponnese.

fix: twenty-four feet high and three palms (about nine inches) in diameter
reason: τριῶν παλαιστῶν: three palms, about nine inches, not a foot.

fix: complete discouragement and famine, partly because of the numbers gathered there and partly because they expected a siege
reason: τὰ μὲν … τὰ δέ covers both conditions; 'discouragement because of the panic' is an invented separate cause.

fix: and because, too, one spell of stormy weather had not yet ended while another was coming on
reason: ἐπισημασία is a star-signalled spell of bad weather; καταλήγειν/ἐπιφέρεσθαι mean ending/coming on, not setting/rising constellations.
ἀντιφιλοδοξοῦντες πρὸς τὸν Ἀσδρούβαν: competing with Hasdrubal for glory, as the next clause confirms; not vying with each other.

fix: along with them he immediately sent Hannibal to the Gauls
reason: μετ᾽ αὐτῶν ἀπέστειλε: Hannibal and Alexon were sent with the loyal officers; no 'his own men' in the Greek.
Polybius's Ἀτάρβας is the Drepana commander conventionally called Adherbal; same person, and Book 1 uses Adherbal throughout.

fix: an internal war awaited the Romans—the one against the people called the Faliscans
reason: ἐξεδέξατο: a war was in store for/followed upon them; 'broke out to receive' garbles the verb. Closest minimal fix.

fix: did not give them up, and they warned those present
reason: οὔτ᾽ ἔδοσαν, προεῖπόν τε: one negated verb plus 'and warned'; 'nor allowed it' is invented.
